Up to 10 resources in parallel can be collected, some resources are more urgently needed than others.
Some resources are required to create tools that are needed to gather other resources (create a custom logic of the dependencies in your game).
After all preferences are collected, your bot starts farming.
Sometimes,  random natural disasters strike and set your bot back.
Whenever some milestones are reached, you are notified.
During farming it is possible to update the list of to be farmed materials (at all times).
After the bot is finished, you should be able to brag to selected friends and/or send them materials.

result.rule: Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

result.rule: When the description says that an autonomous actor (such as a bot) performs activities after a user starts it, and that the user may perform another action at any time while those activities run, or that an external event may interrupt them: Model the user-initiated action or the interrupting event as an event subprocess or a boundary event attached to the actor's activity, placed in the lane of the autonomous actor that performs the activity. Do not model it as a separate subprocess or task in the user's lane, and do not add a separate pool for the actor.

When the description names two roles, one of which supplies choices or requirements that a separate automated agent then acts on to perform the later steps of the same process: Keep all steps of the process in one participant pool. Create one lane for each named role, including the automated agent, and place each start event, task and gateway in the lane of the role that performs it. Put the starting event in the lane of the role that initiates the process, and put the later performed steps in the lane of the automated agent. Do not omit the lanes, and do not split these roles into separate pools.

When the description has a step of one role whose result is passed to a different role, and the receiving role then performs its own described step as a task in its own pool (for example, a role that is asked to act on information or an item another role has sent): Model the receiving step as a task in the receiving role's pool and draw a message flow from the sending step in the sender's pool to that receiving task, with the arrow pointing from sender to receiver. Do not replace this flow with one that ends at a catch event when the receiver's described step is a performed task, and do not reverse the arrow direction.

When the description states that one participant is held until another participant makes something available or arrives, and then describes one or more further actions by the first participant on it, in a stated order: Model the awaited occurrence as an intermediate catch event. Model each described action of the participant as its own task, in the stated order, on the sequence flow after that event. Do not place an end event between the catch event and these tasks, and do not treat the occurrence itself as the completion of the process.
